how: One source mutation applied to the working tree, the named suite run against it, then the file restored before the next row (X14/X15's convention: `before` is the shipped source the row was run against and `after` the text that replaced it). Device rows ran on lease G23-zcs2m, pair-b (iPhone Air / iOS 27 and emulator-5570 / API 35); the filtered gate names satisfy nothing but their own name. Rows marked `organic` are not mutations: they are a new test going red against the real bug before its fix, which is the stronger evidence, and the logs are in `gate.mjs logs --branch task/G23-icon-button`. Rows 1-4 share one build and one run, so one red line is attributed to each of them by which assertion failed.

mutations.mutation: the width option leaves the size configuration, so narrow, uniform and wide are one cached size
redTests: lays every rung and width out at the size the control measured: testID "rung-medium-narrow" (rung-medium-narrow) never reached 48.00x48.00 - last box 52.19x48.00, control measured 48.00x48.00.
mutations.note: Q9 C4's red proof for the key, and the failure is the interesting shape: the `narrow` control was served the `wide` configuration's size, which is what a key collision looks like from JS. The poisoned key and the collision are the same key, so the ladder test is the one that goes red rather than the width-key test — recorded because the report cites the line, not the test name.

mutations.mutation: the control's own name leaves the composition, so the button has no contentDescription
mutations.before:
val labelModifier =
      if (label != null) Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = label } else Modifier
mutations.after:
val labelModifier: Modifier = Modifier
      .also { label?.let { it } }

mutations.mutation: the flip is reported without its event count, so JS cannot tell a fresh write from a stale one
redTests: reverts a toggle JS refused, and shows the value JS wrote: "refusing" never drew displayed=0 - it reports "displayed=1;probes=0;a11y=none".
mutations.note: The handshake's own gate (core-architecture §4): the refusal is JS writing the old value back with a count native must accept, and with every count 0 it is refused instead.

mutations.mutation: the tint is painted as a constant, so a disabled control keeps the pure colour instead of Material's 38% content colour
redTests: draws the glyph in the control content colour, at the size the rung asked for: expected 642 to be +0 // Object.is equality (the `expect(hitsOf('probe-disabled')).toBe(0)` line)
mutations.note: C4's tint row. The probe counts pixels of the exact tint: a correctly dimmed glyph contributes none, a constant-tinted one contributes 642.

mutations.mutation: a glyph that cannot be resolved throws instead of drawing nothing
mutations.run: harness:android:IconButton — the suite could not run
redTests: Test suite failed to run: The app bridge disconnected during test execution. This can happen if the app was killed, crashed, reloaded, or restarted while the test file was running.
mutations.note: C4's missing-drawable row, run alone because a crash takes the whole file with it. The shipped rule is that an unresolvable `androidIcon` draws nothing and reserves nothing; the failure mode it guards against is a control that crashes the app over a name the resource table does not have.

mutations.mutation: the recycle reset skips the glyph slot, so the next owner inherits the previous owner's artwork
redTests: aRecycledModelHandsOnAnEmptyGlyphSlotAndRetiresThePreviousOwnersRead FAILED — java.lang.AssertionError at IconButtonModelTest.kt:190 ("a recycled control draws nothing until its own owner resolves")
mutations.note: C4's recycle row. `androidIcon` is a wire prop that every mount re-sends, so the model's other fields look covered by the reset alone; the slot is the one recycled thing no prop re-sends an answer for. Proved on the JVM because the state is reachable there and the device cannot see a control that was never handed to a second owner.

mutations.mutation: the slot's reset clears the artwork but stops retiring in-flight reads
redTests: aRecycledModelHandsOnAnEmptyGlyphSlotAndRetiresThePreviousOwnersRead FAILED — java.lang.AssertionError at IconButtonModelTest.kt:203 ("a retired read cannot paint the next owner's control")
mutations.note: The second half of the same row, and the reason the test answers the in-flight read with real artwork rather than with null: a null answer lands on `Absent` either way and the assertion would pass for the wrong reason.

mutations.mutation: not a mutation: the container was asked for inside the control's content, which is what the first draft did
mutations.run: harness:android (the branch's first full run) — FAIL
redTests: lays every rung and width out at the size the control measured: expected 48 to be greater than 48
mutations.note: All fifteen configurations came back 48.00x48.00: each M3 composable's own Box is `minimumInteractiveComponentSize().size(smallContainerSize())`, and `Modifier.size` coerces into the constraints it is given, so a container asked for inside the content is measured under the `small` token. Fixed by putting the ask on the control's own modifier.
